refuter_votes.reason: The provision imposes a nationality-based restriction (Bumiputera only) on government procurement bidding for a specific value range. This fits the P2-I3 legal test for a 'set-aside' or 'limitation' triggered by origin/nationality. It is not an outright exclusion of all foreign firms from the entire procurement regime (which would be P2-I1), but a specific bidding limitation. The mapping is legally sound.

The rubric explicitly lists 'bumiputera preference' as a positive cue. The provision requires invitations to be sent only to registered Bumiputera companies, which is a nationality-based set-aside. According to the scoring rubric, a measure directly discriminating against foreign bidders (or non-Bumiputera) scores 1. The mapping correctly identifies this as a P2-I3 indicator with a high score potential. The 'Horizontal' coverage is appropriate as it applies to general supplies/services.

The text states 'hendaklah dipelawa di kalangan syarikat Bumiputera' (shall be invited among Bumiputera companies). The provision is not a mere empowerment clause; it mandates that procurement advertisements must state the implementation of Price Preference for Bumiputera companies (para 9.12(xi)) and restricts supply invitations to local manufacturers (para 9.12(xii)). This constitutes an operative limitation in bidding, satisfying the legal test for P2-I3.

The rubric scores '1' for measures directly discriminating against foreign bidders or based on nationality/origin. The exact text in para 9.12(xi) requires the advertisement to include a 'Kenyataan pelaksanaan Keutamaan Harga kepada syarikat Bumiputera' (Statement of implementation of Price Preference to Bumiputera companies). This textually establishes the existence and application of a nationality-based price preference mechanism in the procurement process, supporting the mapping rationale.
